mcq.QUESTION_DESC: General form of second order PDE in two independent variables \(x\) and \(y\), \(A, B, C, D, E, F, G\) are constants:
A second order linear PDE in two independent variable \(x \) and \(y\) is said to be elliptic, if

sq.ANSWER:
\( ax² + bxy + cy² + dx + ey + f = 0\) -- (3m)

Principal part  \(ax^2+bxy+cy^2\) -- (2m)
sq.QUESTION_DESC:
1. The general second-order algebraic equation in two variables is given by ?
  2. The nature of the curve depends on which part of the equation?

Depending on the sign of the discriminant  \(b^2- 4ac\) ,

  • if \(b^2-4ac > 0\), \(\)the curve traces _________.
  • if \(b^2-4ac = 0\), the curev traces _________.
  • if \(b^2-4ac < 0\), the curve traces _________.

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
For (i): A=4, B=6, C=9. Compute discriminant:  \(B^2 - 4AC = 36 - 144 = -108 < 0\Rightarrow\) elliptic. (2 Marks)
For (ii): A=x^2, B=-2xy, C=y^2. Discriminant: \(4x^2y^2 - 4x^2y^2 = 0 \Rightarrow\) parabolic for all ((x,y) except at origin. (2 Marks)
For (iii): Write as \(c^2u_{xx} - u_{tt} = -\sin(x)\). A=c^2, B=0, C=-1. Discriminant: \(0 - 4(c^2)(-1)=4c^2 > 0 \Rightarrow\) hyperbolic. (2 Marks)
Justify classification: elliptic if \(B^2-4AC<0\), parabolic if =0, hyperbolic if >0. (2 Marks)
Discuss physical interpretation: elliptic (steady state), parabolic (heat/diffusion), hyperbolic (wave/vibration). (3 Marks)
Note: (ii) is parabolic except at origin where coefficients vanish; classify there separately. (2 Marks)
Final classification: (i) elliptic, (ii) parabolic, (iii) hyperbolic. (2 Marks)
lq.QUESTION_DESC:
\(\text{Classify the following PDEs as elliptic, parabolic or hyperbolic and justify your answer:}\)
\(i)\ 4u_{xx} + 6u_{xy} + 9u_{yy} + u_x - u_y = 0.\)
\(ii)\ x^2 u_{xx} - 2xy u_{xy} + y^2 u_{yy} = e^x.\)
\(iii)\ \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} + \sin(x).\)

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
Identify coefficients:\( A = 1-x^2, B = -2xy, C = 1-y^2.\) (1 Mark)
Compute discriminant: \(\text{\(\Delta = B^2 - 4AC = 4x^2y^2 - 4(1-x^2)(1-y^2)\)}\). (2 Marks)
Simplify: \(\Delta = 4[x^2y^2 - (1 - x^2 - y^2 + x^2y^2)] = 4(x^2 + y^2 - 1)\). (3 Marks)
Parabolic if \( \Delta=0\Rightarrow x^2 + y^2 = 1 \)(circle of radius 1). (2 Marks)
Elliptic if \(\Delta<0 \Rightarrow x^2 + y^2 < 1\) (inside the circle). (2 Marks)
Hyperbolic if \( \Delta>0 \Rightarrow x^2 + y^2 > 1\) (outside the circle). (2 Marks)
Discuss boundary: on circle parabolic, inside elliptic, outside hyperbolic. (2 Marks)
Conclusion with region description. (1 Mark)
lq.QUESTION_DESC:
\(​​​​​​​\text{Classify the PDE: } (1 - x^2)u_{xx} - 2xy u_{xy} + (1 - y^2)u_{yy} + x u_x + 3x^2y u_y - 2u = 0.\)

\(\text{Determine regions in the xy-plane where it is elliptic, parabolic, or hyperbolic.}\)
